senses.why: The adjective came straight from Latin minutus, made small, and it kept the literal sense of size while the noun moved off to the clock; English also gives it a long vowel, which is why the two senses sound different.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接来自拉丁语 minutus（变小），保留了字面上的尺寸义，而名词则走去指钟表上的单位；英语还让形容词读长音，所以两种义项听起来不同。

senses.title: Very detailed and precise
senses.definition: done with close attention to small details, as in a minute account or a minute examination
senses.definitionCN: 对细小之处极为留意的，如细致的叙述或细致的检查
senses.example: The report gives a minute account of the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对实验作了极为细致的记述。
senses.why: If something is so small that it needs a close look, then a close look is what the adjective also describes, so from tiny size the word slides to care about tiny detail.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物小到必须凑近才看得清，那么这种凑近的查看本身也能被同一个形容词描述，于是词义从「尺寸极小」滑向「对细处极用心」。

senses.title: The official record of a meeting
senses.definition: the written notes of what was said and decided at a meeting, usually kept in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 会议上发言与决定的书面记录，通常用复数
senses.example: The secretary took the minutes in shorthand.
senses.exampleCN: 秘书用速记做会议记录。
senses.why: Early clerks wrote the record of a meeting in very small script to save paper, and the Latin word for small gave both the script and the record its name, which is why the notes are minutes.
senses.whyCN: 早期文书为了省纸，把会议记录写得很小，拉丁语中表示「小」的词同时给了这种小字和记录本身一个名字，所以记录叫 minutes。

intro.en: Minute carries two histories in one spelling: a Latin adjective meaning made small gave both the clock unit and the adjective, and English separated them by pronunciation.
intro.cn: minute 一个拼写里装着两段历史：拉丁语中表示「变小」的形容词既生出钟表单位，也生出形容词，英语用读音把它们分开了。

items.en: Minutus meant made small, a participle of the verb minuere, to lessen, and it described anything reduced in size.
items.cn: minutus 意为「被弄小的」，是动词 minuere（减少）的分词，用来描述任何被缩小的东西。

items.en: The phrase pars minuta prima, first small part, named one sixtieth of an hour and one sixtieth of a degree, and the small-part word was carried into the unit.
items.cn: 短语 pars minuta prima 意为「第一小部分」，指一小时的六十分之一与一度的六十分之一，这个「小部分」的词后来进入了单位名称。

items.en: Old French used minute for a small written note, especially the clerk's draft of a legal or official record.
items.cn: 古法语用 minute 指小字写的便条，尤指文书对法律或公务记录的草稿。

items.en: Middle English minute named both the sixtieth of an hour and a brief moment, while the adjective small sense entered from written Latin.
items.cn: 中古英语的 minute 既指一小时的六十分之一，也指短暂的片刻；表示「小」的形容词义则从书面拉丁语进入。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun with a short vowel, the adjective with a long vowel, and the plural minutes for the record of a meeting.
items.cn: 现代英语让名词读短音、形容词读长音，并用复数 minutes 指会议记录。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root of smallness through derived adverbs and nouns; the near-meaning group gathers other words for short stretches of time.
note.cn: 形近组顺着表示「小」的拉丁词根，收派生副词与名词；近义组收其他表示短暂时间的词。

entries.definition: In tiny detail; with close attention to small parts.
entries.definitionCN: 以极细的程度；对细部极为留意地。

entries.definition: The quality of being extremely small.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的性质。

entries.definition: Extremely small, or a word form marking smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的；指小的词形。

entries.definition: The Latin verb meaning to lessen, listed here for the root only.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语动词「减少」，此处仅列词根。

entries.definition: A very short period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 极短的一段时间。

entries.definition: A unit of time equal to one sixtieth of a minute.
entries.definitionCN: 等于一分钟六十分之一的时间单位。

entries.definition: A single point in time, or a very brief moment.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻；极短的瞬间。

entries.definition: A period of time, usually short and vague.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，通常短暂而模糊。

normalIntro.en: One Latin adjective for small feeds two separate words, so the family splits between clock time, tiny size and the paper record of a meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「小」的拉丁形容词喂出两条不同的词路，词族因此分到钟表时间、极小尺寸与会议纸面记录。

normal.en: The time unit began as pars minuta prima, the first small part of an hour, so minute literally names a small slice of time.
normal.cn: 这个时间单位起初是 pars minuta prima，即「一小时的第一小部分」，所以 minute 字面上就是时间的一小片。

normal.en: The adjective keeps the Latin sense of minutus, made small, and English marks it with a long vowel so the ear can tell it from the clock word.
normal.cn: 形容词保留了拉丁语 minutus（变小）的意思，英语用长音标记它，让耳朵能把它与钟表那个词分开。

normal.en: Minutes of a meeting were first notes written in small script, which is why the official record shares the spelling of the small adjective.
normal.cn: 会议记录最初是用小字写下的笔记，所以正式记录与小这个形容词共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: Minutely and minuteness belong to the small adjective rather than to the time noun, and their vowels show which branch they come from.
normal.cn: minutely 与 minuteness 属于「小」的形容词，而不是时间名词，它们的元音显示了自己来自哪一支。

normal.en: Diminutive comes from the same Latin verb minuere, to lessen, so the whole family keeps returning to shrinking.
normal.cn: diminutive 出自同一个拉丁动词 minuere（减少），整个词族不断回到「缩小」这个动作。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face cut into sixty thin slices, then one slice held up close enough to show its scratches.
abstract.cn: 想象钟面被切成六十片薄片，然后取一片凑近到能看清上面的划痕。

abstract.en: The same word measures the hour and the speck of dust: smallness is the thread joining the clock to the microscope.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既量一小时，也量一粒尘：小是把钟表与显微镜串起来的那根线。

abstract.en: A meeting becomes a few written pages, and those pages are named after the smallness of the handwriting that saved paper.
abstract.cn: 一场会议变成几页纸，而这几页纸得名于当初为省纸而写的小字。

examples.en: The train leaves in a minute.
examples.cn: 列车一分钟后开。

examples.en: The letters on the coin were minute and hard to read.
examples.cn: 硬币上的字母极小，很难辨认。

examples.en: She took the minutes at every board meeting.
examples.cn: 每次董事会都由她做记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷你特」——迷你的本子很小，翻一页只花一分钟；记住 minute 既指分钟，也指微小的。

root: 拉丁语 minutus（变小，出自 minuere「减少」）；时间义来自 pars minuta prima（一小时的第一小部分），形容词义直接来自 minutus；会议记录义经古法语 minute（小字记录）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small piece of the hour; the senses divide into the clock unit, the vague short moment, the tiny size kept by the adjective, the close detail that size demands, and the small-script record of a meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「小时里的一小片」；义项分到钟表单位、模糊的短暂片刻、形容词保留的极小尺寸、小尺寸所要求的细致，以及用小字写成的会议记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small clock hand sweeping a circle cut into sixty narrow slices.
core.cn: 核心意象：小小的钟表指针扫过被切成六十个窄格的圆盘。

branches.en: a clock face divided into sixty slices
branches.cn: 钟面被分成六十格

branches.en: someone holding a door and saying just a moment
branches.cn: 有人扶住门说再等一下

branches.en: a crack too thin for the eye to catch
branches.cn: 细得眼睛看不见的裂纹

branches.en: a page of notes on the smallest parts of a test
branches.cn: 一页记着实验最细处的笔记

branches.en: a clerk writing the meeting in tiny script
branches.cn: 文书用小字记下会议

intro.en: Latin words for small and to lessen supply the stem, and English suffixes build the adverb, the quality noun and the family word for a small form.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「小」与「减少」的词提供词干，英语后缀则造出副词、性质名词，以及与「指小」相关的词族成员。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: first small part of an hour

definition_zh: 奇迹；神迹；奇迹般的事；非凡成就；典范
definition_en: an extraordinary event believed to come from divine power; also any astonishing achievement, or a wonderful example of a craft
core_image: 干涸的石池底忽然涌出清水，围观的人一时说不出话
scene: 旱季的村口，人们围着那口多年见底的老井，清晨时井底竟重新有了水。The villagers called the refilled well a miracle.
sceneCN: 这里是「奇迹、神迹」（第 1 个义项：超出常理、被认为是神力所致的事）；句意为村民把重新蓄水的老井称作奇迹。图中可辨识物件：老井、水桶、围观的人群。

derivatives.zh: 由 miracle 词干加 -ous 构成，义为「奇迹般的；不可思议的」
由 miraculous 加 -ly 构成，义为「奇迹般地」
由 miracle 与 worker 复合，义为「创造奇迹的人」

senses.title: An event believed to come from divine power
senses.definition: an extraordinary event that cannot be explained by natural laws and is believed to be caused by divine power
senses.definitionCN: 无法用自然规律解释、被认为是神力所致的非凡事件
senses.example: Pilgrims came to the shrine hoping to witness a miracle.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者来到圣殿，希望能亲眼见到一次神迹。
senses.why: Latin miraculum named the thing that makes a person wonder, and religious writing applied it to events that only divine power could account for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miraculum 指「让人惊奇的东西」，宗教写作把它用在只有神力才能解释的事件上。

senses.title: An astonishing escape or achievement
senses.definition: a remarkable outcome that seemed impossible, such as a narrow escape or an achievement against the odds
senses.definitionCN: 看似不可能却发生了的非凡结果，如死里逃生或逆境中的成就
senses.example: It was a miracle that no one was hurt in the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车事故中没有人受伤，真是奇迹。
senses.why: Once the word named what natural law cannot explain, it easily extended to any result that defies expectation, above all a survival nobody thought possible.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指自然规律解释不了的事，它就很容易扩展到任何违背预期的结果，尤其是原本认为不可能的幸存。

senses.title: A wonderful example of a craft
senses.definition: a thing so excellent or finely made that it fills the observer with wonder, as in a miracle of engineering
senses.definitionCN: 精巧或优异到让观者惊叹的事物，如工程上的奇迹
senses.example: The old bridge is a miracle of stonework and patience.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古桥是石工与耐心的奇迹。
senses.why: A structure that makes engineers wonder deserves the same word as a holy wonder, because wonder is the shared response rather than the cause.
senses.whyCN: 让工程师惊叹的建筑配得上与神圣奇观相同的词，因为共同点是观者的惊叹，而不是成因。

intro.en: Miracle goes back to a Latin verb meaning to wonder, whose noun named the thing that caused the wonder, and it entered English through French religious writing.
intro.cn: miracle 可追到一个意为「惊奇」的拉丁动词，其名词指引起惊奇的那个东西，再经法语宗教文本进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to wonder at or to be amazed by something; the deeper origin of the verb is generally regarded as uncertain.
items.cn: mirari 意为对某物感到惊奇、惊叹；这个动词更早的来源一般认为不确定。

items.en: Miraculum named an object of wonder, a marvel, and early Christian Latin narrowed it to an event beyond nature.
items.cn: miraculum 指令人惊奇之物、奇观，早期基督教拉丁语把它收窄为超自然的事件。

items.en: Old French miracle meant a holy wonder and also named the religious plays staged around such stories.
items.cn: 古法语 miracle 指神圣的奇事，也用来称呼围绕这类故事上演的宗教剧。

items.en: Middle English miracle covered both the holy event and the tale told about it, and the drama sense slowly faded.
items.cn: 中古英语的 miracle 既指神圣事件，也指讲述它的事迹，戏剧的意思后来慢慢消失。

items.en: Modern English widened the word to astonishing escapes and to excellent works, so a bridge can now be called a miracle.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到惊人的脱险与出色的作品，于是一座桥如今也能被称作奇迹。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin verb for wondering; the near-meaning group collects other names for astonishing things.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「惊奇」动词上的词；近义组收其他表示惊人事物的名称。

entries.definition: Brought about as if by a miracle; astonishing.
entries.definitionCN: 仿佛由奇迹促成的；令人惊叹的。

entries.definition: An optical illusion, such as water appearing in a desert.
entries.definitionCN: 光学幻景，如沙漠中看似出现的水。

entries.definition: To regard someone or something with wonder and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 带着惊叹与赞许地看待某人或某物。

entries.definition: A reflective glass, or something that shows a faithful image.
entries.definitionCN: 反光的镜子，或忠实映现事物的东西。

entries.definition: A feeling of surprise and awe at something remarkable.
entries.definitionCN: 面对非凡事物时的惊讶与敬畏。

entries.definition: A wonderful thing, or to be filled with wonder at it.
entries.definitionCN: 奇妙的事物；对其感到惊叹。

entries.definition: Something extraordinary, often a person with exceptional talent.
entries.definitionCN: 非凡之物，常指天赋异禀的人。

entries.definition: A fact or event that can be observed, especially an unusual one.
entries.definitionCN: 可观察到的事实或事件，尤指不寻常的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb for wondering stands behind the whole family, so miracle, mirage, mirror and admire all keep a trace of awe.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「惊奇」的拉丁动词支撑着整个词族，所以 miracle、mirage、mirror 与 admire 都留着惊叹的痕迹。

normal.en: Mirari is Latin for to wonder, and miraculum is the thing that makes the wondering happen.
normal.cn: mirari 在拉丁语中意为「惊奇」，miraculum 就是引起这份惊奇的那个东西。

normal.en: Miracle reached English through Old French, where it already meant a holy wonder rather than any surprise.
normal.cn: miracle 经古法语进入英语，在法语里它已经指神圣的奇事，而不是随便什么意外。

normal.en: Mirage, mirror and admire descend from the same verb, which is why a desert illusion and a looking glass feel related to wonder.
normal.cn: mirage、mirror 与 admire 出自同一个动词，所以沙漠幻景与镜子在语感上都与惊奇有关。

normal.en: Miracle play was the medieval name for drama on holy subjects, a sense that English later dropped.
normal.cn: miracle play 是中世纪对宗教题材戏剧的称呼，这层意思后来被英语舍弃。

normal.en: The plural miracles stays countable: the word names single events, not a general mood of awe.
normal.cn: 复数 miracles 保持可数：这个词指一个个单独的事件，而不是笼统的敬畏气氛。

abstract.en: Picture a dry stone basin filling overnight while a crowd stands speechless.
abstract.cn: 想象干涸的石池一夜之间蓄满水，人群围着说不出话。

abstract.en: A word born from wonder can end up naming a bridge, because awe does not ask what caused the thing it admires.
abstract.cn: 一个从惊奇里生出的词最后可以指一座桥，因为惊叹并不追问被赞叹之物的成因。

abstract.en: What counts as a miracle depends on what a community believes is possible, so the word always carries a shared limit.
abstract.cn: 什么算奇迹取决于一个群体认为什么才可能，所以这个词总带着一条共同的边界。

examples.en: The villagers called the refilled well a miracle.
examples.cn: 村民把重新蓄水的老井称作奇迹。

examples.en: It was a miracle that no one was hurt in the crash.
examples.cn: 撞车事故中没有人受伤，真是奇迹。

examples.en: The bridge is a miracle of engineering.
examples.cn: 这座桥是工程上的奇迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米拉可」——米拉可一挥手，干井冒出水，众人称奇；记住 miracle 是奇迹。

definition_zh: 镜子；镜面；写照；反映；映照
definition_en: a piece of glass with a reflective coating that shows images; also something that gives a faithful picture of a situation, and to show or match something as a mirror does
core_image: 晨光里的一面镜子，把窗前的人原样照回来
scene: 清晨的走廊上，她把外套领子翻正，又抬手理了理头发。She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜子」（第 1 个义项：能照出影像的玻璃物件）；句意为面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。图中可辨识物件：镜子、衣领、走廊灯。

derivatives.zh: 由动词 mirror 加 -ing 构成，义为「镜像；反映」
由动词 mirror 加 -ed 构成，义为「装有镜子的；映出的」
由 mirror 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无镜的」，多指相机结构

senses.title: A glass surface that shows a reflection
senses.definition: a piece of glass or polished surface with a reflective coating that shows the image of what stands before it
senses.definitionCN: 镀有反光层的玻璃或抛光表面，能照出面前事物的影像
senses.example: She checked her collar in the mirror before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她对着镜子整理衣领。
senses.why: The word came through Old French from a Vulgar Latin noun for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经古法语来自一个表示「照人用的玻璃」的俗拉丁名词，后者建于动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，所以物件是按它招来的那道目光命名的。

senses.title: A faithful picture of a situation
senses.definition: a person or thing that shows a situation, a period or a mood exactly as it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某种局面、时代或情绪如实呈现出来的人或事物
senses.example: The novel is a mirror of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是那个时代的写照。
senses.why: Because a mirror returns an exact image rather than a flattering one, writers use it for anything that shows a situation without distortion, and a novel can serve as that surface.
senses.whyCN: 镜子给出的是准确而非讨好的影像，作家便用它指任何不失真地呈现局面的东西，一部小说也能充当这样一面镜面。

senses.title: To show an image as a mirror does
senses.definition: to show the image of something, the way a still surface reflects what stands beside it
senses.definitionCN: 像平静表面那样把旁边的事物影像呈现出来
senses.example: The lake mirrored the pines along the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面映出岸边的松树。
senses.why: The verb was simply the noun turned into an action, so to mirror is to do what a mirror does: send back the image of whatever stands before it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把名词直接变成动作，所以 to mirror 就是做镜子所做的事：把面前事物的影像送回原处。

senses.title: To match or correspond closely
senses.definition: to be very similar to something else, so that the two seem to copy each other
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为相似，看上去像彼此复制出来的一样
senses.example: The vote mirrored the national trend.
senses.exampleCN: 投票结果与全国趋势一致。
senses.why: When two patterns look identical, one seems to be the reflection of the other, so the verb widened from reflecting light to reflecting behaviour, numbers and opinions.
senses.whyCN: 当两种走势看起来一模一样，其中一个就像是另一个的倒影，于是这个动词从映出光线扩展到映出行为、数字与观点。

intro.en: Mirror comes from a Vulgar Latin name for a looking glass, built on the verb mirari, to look at or wonder at, and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: mirror 来自俗拉丁语中「照人用的玻璃」这一名称，建立在动词 mirari（注视、惊叹）之上，再经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to look at with wonder, and the looking and the wondering were not separated in the verb.
items.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，在这个动词里，「看」与「惊叹」并没有分开。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin noun, reconstructed as miratorium, named the thing one looks into; the form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语中有一个表示「供人照看的器物」的名词，学界重构为 miratorium；这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Old French mirour carried the noun into ordinary use for the polished metal or glass a person looks into.
items.cn: 古法语 mirour 把这个名词带入日常用法，指人们照看的抛光金属或玻璃。

items.en: Middle English mirrour kept the extra vowel of the French form and also used the word for moral examples and ideal portraits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mirrour 保留了法语形式里多出的元音，也用这个词指道德榜样与理想化的画像。

items.en: Modern English shortened the spelling to mirror, formed a matching verb, and pushed the word into talk about trends, reports and behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写缩成 mirror，造出与之相配的动词，并把这个词推进到关于趋势、报告与行为的说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for looking and wondering; the near-meaning group gathers words for reflections and for the surfaces that produce them.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词展开；近义组收表示影像以及产生影像的表面的词。

entries.definition: An optical illusion in which water seems to appear in the distance.
entries.definitionCN: 远处看似有水的一种光学幻景。

entries.definition: To look at someone with wonder and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 带着惊叹与赞许地看某人。

entries.definition: An astonishing event believed to come from divine power.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为是神力所致的惊人之事。

entries.definition: The act of reflecting an image, or of copying another's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 映出影像的行为，或模仿他人行为的过程。

entries.definition: The image of something seen in a mirror or on water.
entries.definitionCN: 镜中或水面看到的事物的影像。

entries.definition: A hard, transparent material, or a mirror made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬透明的材料，或用它制成的镜子。

entries.definition: A picture or likeness of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 某人某物的图像或相似物。

entries.definition: To send back light or an image, or to show a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 把光或影像送回；反映某种情况。

normalIntro.en: The Latin verb for looking and wondering gives the noun, and the noun then turns into a verb, so the family keeps moving between the glass and the act of copying.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「看」与「惊叹」的动词生出名词，名词又变成动词，于是词族在镜面与复制这个动作之间来回移动。

normal.en: Mirari means to look at with wonder, and a mirror was first a looking glass, so the object is named for the gaze it invites.
normal.cn: mirari 意为带着惊叹地看，而 mirror 起初就是照人的玻璃，所以这个物件按它招来的目光得名。

normal.en: Mirror, miracle, mirage and admire share that Latin verb, which is why looking and wondering sit close together in this family.
normal.cn: mirror、miracle、mirage 与 admire 共用那个拉丁动词，所以看与惊叹在这个词族里挨得很近。

normal.en: The noun came first, and to mirror is a later verb made by simply treating the object as an action.
normal.cn: 名词先出现，to mirror 是后来把这个物件直接当作动作来用才有的动词。

normal.en: Mirror image names a copy reversed left to right, the most literal use of the noun in front of another noun.
normal.cn: mirror image 指左右颠倒的复制影像，是名词放在另一个名词前最字面的用法。

normal.en: The phrase a mirror of the times still demands a faithful picture, not a flattering one.
normal.cn: a mirror of the times 这一说法仍然要求如实呈现，而不是美化。

abstract.en: Picture a still lake at dawn returning the trees exactly, without adding or hiding anything.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时平静的湖面把树影原样送回，既不增添也不隐藏。

abstract.en: A mirror can flatter or accuse, but it cannot lie about the shape in front of it; the word keeps that demand for accuracy.
abstract.cn: 镜子可以讨好也可以揭短，但它无法对面前的形状说谎；这个词一直保留着这份准确的要求。

abstract.en: To mirror someone is to become their reflection, which is why imitation and understanding can look the same from outside.
abstract.cn: to mirror 某人就是成为他的倒影，所以模仿与理解从外面看往往一模一样。

examples.en: She checked her collar in the mirror.
examples.cn: 她对着镜子整理衣领。

examples.en: The report mirrors what workers have been saying for years.

sensesIntro.en: The core is a surface that returns an image; the senses divide into the glass itself, the faithful picture it stands for, the act of sending back an image, and the matching of two patterns.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把影像送回原处的表面」；义项分到玻璃物件本身、它所代表的如实写照、送回影像的动作，以及两种走势的彼此吻合。

core.cn: 核心意象：晨光中的一面镜子，把镜前的人原样送回。

definition_zh: 误解；错误观念；错误认识
definition_en: a wrong belief or idea that someone holds because a fact, a word or a situation has been understood incorrectly
core_image: 一张画错方向的路线图，被人当成真的，越走越远
scene: 课堂上，一个学生把地图上的南北认反了，照着这张图走了很久，离目的地越来越远。Many people hold the misconception that we use only a small part of our brains.
sceneCN: 这里是「错误观念」（第 1 个义项：被当成真的错误想法）；句意为很多人误以为我们只用了大脑的一小部分。图中可辨识物件：认反的地图、走远的身影、远处的目的地。

pos.zh: 误解；错误观念；错误认识

derivatives.zh: 由 mis- 与 conceive 构成，义为「误解；构想错误」
由 misconceive 加 -ed 构成，义为「理解错误的；设计不当的」

senses.title: A mistaken belief held as true
senses.definition: a wrong belief that a person accepts as true because something has been understood incorrectly
senses.definitionCN: 因为把某件事理解错了，而把错误的想法当成真的
senses.example: It is a misconception that goldfish remember nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 认为金鱼什么都记不住，是一种误解。
senses.why: Conception names the mind's act of forming an idea, and mis- marks that act as a wrong turn, so the word points at an idea built on a faulty grasp rather than at a single mistaken fact.
senses.whyCN: conception 指头脑中形成想法的动作，mis- 把这个动作标成走偏的一步，所以这个词指向建立在错误理解上的想法，而不只是一条记错的事实。

senses.title: A false idea shared by many people
senses.definition: an inaccurate idea that circulates widely among people and is repeated without being checked
senses.definitionCN: 在人群中广泛流传、被反复转述却无人核对的错误看法
senses.example: The belief that sugar makes children hyperactive is a widespread misconception.
senses.exampleCN: 认为糖会让孩子过度活跃，是一种普遍的错误看法。
senses.why: An idea spreads when many minds conceive it in the same way, so a private mistake turns into a public one; the word then names the shared version rather than one person's confusion.
senses.whyCN: 当许多头脑以同样的方式形成同一个想法，这个想法就会传开，个人的错误便变成公共的错误；于是这个词指大家共同持有的那个版本，而不是某一个人的糊涂。

senses.title: A wrong reading of a rule, word or text
senses.definition: a mistaken understanding of what a rule, a word or a piece of writing actually requires or says
senses.definitionCN: 对规则、词语或文字实际要求或所说内容产生的错误理解
senses.example: His misconception of the contract led him to sign away the rights.
senses.exampleCN: 他对合同的误解使他签字放弃了权利。
senses.why: If conception is the mind taking hold of a thing, it can take hold of a sentence as well as of the world, so misconceiving a clause produces the same kind of wrong possession.
senses.whyCN: 如果 conception 是头脑抓住一件事，那么它既能抓住世界，也能抓住一句话；把一条款理解错，就等于以同样的方式抓错了东西。

intro.en: Misconception joins an Old English prefix meaning wrong with a Latin noun for the act of forming an idea in the mind.
intro.cn: misconception 由一个表示「错误」的古英语前缀与一个表示「在心中形成想法」的拉丁名词组合而成。

items.en: The prefix mis- already meant wrong, badly or amiss in Old English, and it was added freely to verbs and nouns.
items.cn: 古英语中的前缀 mis- 已表示错误、不当、出了偏差，可以自由地加在动词和名词前面。

items.en: Concipere joined com-, meaning together, to capere, to take, and meant to take hold of something in the mind.
items.cn: concipere 由表示「共同」的 com- 与表示「拿取」的 capere 组合而成，意为在头脑中把握住某物。

items.en: Conceptio named the act of conceiving and also the thing conceived, and English borrowed it as conception.
items.cn: conceptio 既指构想这个动作，也指被构想出来的东西，英语借入后写作 conception。

items.en: English conception covers both the forming of an idea and the beginning of a pregnancy, because both are a taking hold of something new.
items.cn: 英语的 conception 既指形成想法，也指怀孕的开始，因为两者都是把某种新东西接住、握住。

items.en: Modern English put mis- in front of conception, so the word names an idea taken hold of in the wrong way.
items.cn: 现代英语把 mis- 放在 conception 前面，于是这个词指以错误方式把握住的想法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with mis- or on Latin conception; the near-meaning group gathers words for wrong understanding and for ideas that are not true.
note.cn: 形近组收带 mis- 的词以及建立在拉丁语 conception 上的词；近义组收表示错误理解以及不真实想法的词。

entries.definition: To understand something wrongly; built with mis- and conceive.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事理解错；由 mis- 与 conceive 构成。

entries.definition: The forming of an idea in the mind, or the beginning of a pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成想法，或怀孕的开始。

entries.definition: A wrong way of seeing or understanding something, built with mis- and perception.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的错误看法或理解，由 mis- 与 perception 构成。

entries.definition: A mistaken understanding of a situation or of what someone means.
entries.definitionCN: 对某种情况或他人意思的错误理解。

entries.definition: A failure to understand something correctly, or a small disagreement caused by this.
entries.definitionCN: 没能正确理解某事，或由此引起的小争执。

entries.definition: A false belief, or a piece of reasoning that does not hold.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的想法，或站不住脚的推理。

entries.definition: A false idea or impression, often one that the mind finds pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的想法或印象，常指让头脑觉得愉快的那种。

entries.definition: A widely repeated story or belief that is not true.
entries.definitionCN: 广为流传却不真实的故事或看法。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Germanic prefix for wrongness and a Latin noun for conceiving; its family keeps returning to ideas formed, held and passed on in the wrong shape.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「错误」的日耳曼语前缀和表示「构想」的拉丁名词构成，同族词反复回到被错误地形成、持有并传播的想法。

normal.en: Mis- means wrong and conception means the forming of an idea, so a misconception is an idea formed the wrong way.
normal.cn: mis- 表示错误，conception 表示形成想法，所以 misconception 就是以错误方式形成的想法。

normal.en: Conception comes from Latin capere, to take; a misconception is an idea taken hold of before anyone checks it.
normal.cn: conception 来自拉丁语 capere（拿取）；misconception 就是还没核对就被抓住的想法。

normal.en: Misconceive is the verb, and misconception is the noun that names the result of conceiving wrongly.
normal.cn: misconceive 是动词，misconception 是名词，指错误构想之后留下的结果。

normal.en: Misperception repeats the same pattern with perception instead of conception, and both describe a wrong grasp of something.
normal.cn: misperception 用 perception 替换 conception，重复了同样的构词方式，两个词都指对某物的错误把握。

normal.en: The word is used of ideas rather than of the senses: we say a misconception about a subject, not a misconception of a sound.
normal.cn: 这个词用于想法而不是感官：我们说对某个主题的误解，而不说对一种声音的误解。

abstract.en: A wrong map carried confidently is the whole picture of a misconception: the traveller is lost in the drawing, not in the land.
abstract.cn: 一张被自信地带着的错误地图就是 misconception 的全部画面：旅人不是迷失在土地上，而是迷失在图纸里。

abstract.en: An error becomes a misconception when it is held as true, which is why the word sounds more settled than a simple mistake.
abstract.cn: 错误一旦被当成真的持有，就成了 misconception，所以这个词听起来比单纯的差错更稳固。

abstract.en: Because the word names the mind's wrong taking hold, correcting one is less about adding facts than about loosening a grip.
abstract.cn: 因为这个词指头脑抓错了东西，纠正它不是往头脑里添事实，而更像是把抓得太紧的手松开。

examples.en: It is a misconception that goldfish remember nothing.
examples.cn: 认为金鱼什么都记不住，是一种误解。

examples.en: The belief that sugar makes children hyperactive is a widespread misconception.
examples.cn: 认为糖会让孩子过度活跃，是一种普遍的错误看法。

examples.en: His misconception of the contract led him to sign away the rights.
examples.cn: 他对合同的误解使他签字放弃了权利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米斯康塞普」——米斯把一捆想法接错了线头，整捆都亮成了错的；记住 misconception 是错误观念。

root: 古英语前缀 mis-（错误、不当）加拉丁语 concipere（com- 共同 + capere 抓取，意为「在心中把握」）构成 conceptio（构想），再进入英语为 conception；misconception 即「把握错了的构想」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an idea formed in the wrong way; the senses divide into a private mistaken belief, a widely shared false idea, and a wrong reading of a text or rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是以错误方式形成的想法；义项分为个人持有的错误信念、众人共享的错误看法，以及对文字或规则的错误理解。

scene: 冬天的雨下了一整天，屋檐漏风，一个人裹着湿透的外套坐在台阶上，肩膀一直抖。The refugees spent a miserable night in the leaking tent.
sceneCN: 这里是「痛苦的、悲惨的」（第 1 个义项：身心都很难受）；句意为难民们在一顶漏雨的帐篷里度过了一个悲惨的夜晚。图中可辨识物件：漏风的屋檐、湿透的外套、发抖的肩膀。

pos.zh: 痛苦的；悲惨的；恶劣的；破旧的；少得可怜的

senses.title: Extremely unhappy and distressed
senses.definition: feeling very unhappy, hopeless or lonely, especially over a stretch of time rather than for a moment
senses.definitionCN: 感到非常不快、无望或孤独，尤指持续一段时间而非一时
senses.example: She felt miserable after the argument and could not sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后她心里难受，睡不着觉。
senses.why: Latin miser named a person at the bottom of fortune, so the adjective begins with an inner state rather than with the weather or the room around the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miser 指一个沦落到命运底层的人，所以这个形容词的起点是人的内心状态，而不是他周围的天气或房间。

senses.title: Very unpleasant to live through or experience
senses.definition: of weather, conditions or an event, so bad that it makes people deeply uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 指天气、条件或事件坏到让人非常难受
senses.example: The team played on through miserable weather.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在恶劣的天气里继续比赛。
senses.why: Once the word names a wretched person, it can name the conditions that produce that wretchedness, so the cause takes the same adjective as the effect.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能形容一个可怜人，它也就能形容造成这种可怜处境的条件，于是原因和结果共用了同一个形容词。

senses.title: Of very poor quality or in a bad state
senses.definition: of a place or thing, inadequate, shabby and depressing to be in or to use
senses.definitionCN: 指地方或物品简陋、破败，待在里面或使用它让人沮丧
senses.example: They lived in a miserable little room above a shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在商店楼上的一间破旧小屋。
senses.why: A dwelling that makes its occupants wretched earns the same word, so the misery of the person is transferred to the object that houses him.
senses.whyCN: 让住户痛苦的住处会得到同一个形容词，人的痛苦因此被转移到了容纳他的物件上。

senses.title: Pitifully small in amount
senses.definition: of a sum of money or an amount, so small that it seems unfair or almost insulting
senses.definitionCN: 指金额或数量小得不公平、几乎带侮辱意味
senses.example: He was paid a miserable sum for a whole week of work.
senses.exampleCN: 他干了一整周的活，拿到的报酬少得可怜。
senses.why: The word measures the distance between what a person needs and what is given; an amount that leaves the receiver wretched is called miserable by the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量的是人的需要与实际所得之间的距离；一笔让领取者陷入可怜处境的钱，按同样的逻辑就被叫作 miserable。

intro.en: Miserable comes from the Latin adjective miser, which named a person in wretched circumstances, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: miserable 来自拉丁语形容词 miser，本指身处悲惨境地的人，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Miser described someone wretched, pitiable or unfortunate, and it could also describe the circumstances that made a person so.
items.cn: miser 形容一个人悲惨、可怜、不幸，也能形容把人逼到这种境地的环境。

items.en: Miserabilis meant pitiable or causing pity, built from miser with the suffix -abilis, able to be.
items.cn: miserabilis 意为值得同情、令人怜悯的，由 miser 加表示「可被……的」后缀 -abilis 构成。

items.en: The verb miserari meant to pity or to bewail, and it kept the same root alive across the family.
items.cn: 动词 miserari 意为同情、哀叹，让同一个词根在整个词族中延续下来。

items.en: Old French took miserabilis as miserable, meaning wretched and deserving of pity, and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语把 miserabilis 写作 miserable，意为悲惨、值得同情，并把它传入英语。

items.en: Modern English widened the word from a pitiable person to bad weather, poor rooms and insultingly small sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从「可怜的人」扩展到恶劣的天气、破旧的房间以及少得带侮辱意味的钱。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on Latin miser plus one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for unhappiness and for bleak conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语 miser 上的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示不快乐与荒凉处境的词。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin adjective for a wretched person; its family keeps returning to suffering, to the conditions that cause it, and to things that fall far short.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个形容可怜人的拉丁语形容词上，同族词反复回到痛苦、造成痛苦的环境，以及远远不够的东西。

normal.en: Miser in Latin named a wretched person, so miserable describes a person at the bottom of fortune before it describes weather.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 miser 指不幸的人，所以 miserable 先形容命运底部的人，之后才形容天气。

normal.en: The suffix -abilis in miserabilis marks what deserves pity, and French turned that adjective into the form English borrowed.
normal.cn: miserabilis 中的 -abilis 标记「值得同情」，法语把这个形容词变成英语借入的形式。

normal.en: Miserable keeps the same root as misery and miserly, though the three words went in different directions.
normal.cn: miserable 与 misery、miserly 同根，但这三个词各自走向了不同的意思。

normal.en: English says more miserable and most miserable rather than adding -er, because the adjective is too long for the short ending.
normal.cn: 英语说 more miserable 与 most miserable，而不加 -er，因为这个形容词太长，容不下短词尾。

normal.en: The word moves from a person to a room or a wage, so bad conditions and small amounts both inherit the same feeling.
normal.cn: 这个词从人移到房间或工资，于是恶劣的条件与微薄的数额都继承了同一种感受。

abstract.en: A wet coat under a leaking eave is the whole picture: misery felt on the skin before it is ever named.
abstract.cn: 漏屋檐下一件湿透的外套就是全部画面：苦难先是贴在皮肤上，然后才被叫出名字。

abstract.en: Miserable weather and a miserable wage feel alike because both leave a person with too little to live on.
abstract.cn: 恶劣的天气与少得可怜的工资感觉相似，因为两者都让人所获太少，难以度日。

abstract.en: The word turns a comparison into a feeling: whatever falls far below what a person needs is called miserable.
abstract.cn: 这个词把比较变成感受：凡是远低于一个人所需的东西，都被叫作 miserable。

examples.cn: 难民们在一顶漏雨的帐篷里度过了一个悲惨的夜晚。

examples.en: The team played on through miserable weather.

examples.en: He was paid a miserable sum for a whole week of work.

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person made wretched; the senses spread from that inner state to the conditions that cause it, to shabby places and things, and to amounts that fall far short.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个陷入悲惨处境的人；义项从这种内心状态扩到造成它的环境、破败的场所与物件，以及远远不够的数额。

scene: 屋子里没有生火，雨点一直敲着窗，一个人蜷在角落，把旧毯子拉到下巴。Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.

senses.title: Great unhappiness or suffering
senses.definition: a state of deep unhappiness and pain, especially one that lasts over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 深深的痛苦与难受，尤指持续很久的状态
senses.example: Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。
senses.why: Latin miseria named wretchedness as a condition, so misery begins as a place a person is stuck in rather than as a mood that passes through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miseria 把悲惨说成一种处境，所以 misery 起初是一个人被困住的地方，而不是一阵会过去的心情。

senses.title: A cause or source of hardship
senses.definition: something such as poverty, illness or loss that brings suffering to people
senses.definitionCN: 贫穷、疾病或丧失之类给人带来痛苦的事
senses.example: The flood brought misery to hundreds of villages.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水给数百个村庄带来了苦难。
senses.why: Once miseria names the condition, the things that produce it can take the same word, because English often lets a cause borrow the name of its effect.
senses.whyCN: miseria 一旦指这种处境，制造这种处境的事物也能用同一个词，因为英语常让原因借用结果的名字。

senses.title: A person who complains all the time
senses.definition: in informal British use, someone who is habitually gloomy and complains about everything
senses.definitionCN: 英国口语用法，指一贯阴郁、对什么都抱怨的人
senses.example: Don't be such a misery and come to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 别这么爱抱怨了，来参加聚会吧。
senses.why: The word moves from the feeling to the person who carries it into a room; a misery is someone whose company spreads the very state the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从感受转到把感受带进房间的人；一个 misery 就是那种一在场就把这种状态扩散开来的人。

intro.en: Misery comes from Latin miseria, the noun for wretchedness built on miser, and it reached English by way of Old French.
intro.cn: misery 来自拉丁语 miseria，即建立在 miser 之上、表示悲惨处境的名称，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Miseria named wretchedness, hardship and distress, and it was formed directly on miser, the word for a wretched person.
items.cn: miseria 意为悲惨、困苦、痛苦，直接由表示可怜人的 miser 构成。

items.en: Miser described someone unhappy, pitiable or living in bad circumstances, and it supplied the root for the whole family.
items.cn: miser 形容一个人不快乐、可怜或境遇糟糕，为整个词族提供了词根。

items.en: Old French took miseria as misere, meaning distress and hardship, and passed it on to English.
items.cn: 古法语把 miseria 写作 misere，意为痛苦与困苦，并把它传给英语。

items.en: Middle English misery covered both the state of suffering and the events that caused it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 misery 既指受苦的状态，也指造成痛苦的事件。

items.en: Modern English kept the serious sense and added an informal one for a person who complains without end.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了严肃的义项，又增加了一个口语义，指没完没了抱怨的人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin miser and two neighbours that only share its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for suffering and for deep sorrow.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个拉丁词 miser 上的词，以及两个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示受苦与深切悲伤的词。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for wretchedness; its family keeps returning to the state of suffering, the events that cause it, and the people who carry it into a room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词上，同族词反复回到受苦的状态、造成痛苦的事件，以及把痛苦带进房间的人。

normal.en: Miseria is Latin for wretchedness, and it was built on miser, the word for a wretched person.
normal.cn: miseria 是拉丁语中表示悲惨的词，建立在表示可怜人的 miser 上。

normal.en: Misery keeps the same root as miserable, but the noun names the state while the adjective names the person or thing inside it.
normal.cn: misery 与 miserable 同根，但名词指状态，形容词指处在状态里的人或物。

normal.en: The plural miseries names specific hardships, because a long state of suffering is usually made of many separate blows.
normal.cn: 复数 miseries 指一桩桩具体的不幸，因为长期的受苦通常由许多次打击组成。

normal.en: The phrase 「put someone out of their misery」 first meant to end a creature's suffering, and it now also means to end someone's suspense.
normal.cn: 「put someone out of their misery」起初指结束一个生灵的痛苦，现在也指让某人不必再猜。

normal.en: 「Misery loves company」 is an old saying that treats sorrow as something looking for other people to sit beside.
normal.cn: 「misery loves company」是一句老话，把悲伤看成会去找别人来陪坐的东西。

abstract.en: A cold room with a dying lamp is misery as a place a person cannot leave, not as a mood that passes.
abstract.cn: 一间冷屋子加上一盏将灭的灯，就是 misery：它是人离不开的地方，而不是会过去的心情。

abstract.en: Because the noun names both the feeling and its causes, a flood, a debt and a long illness can all be called miseries.
abstract.cn: 因为这个名词既指感受也指成因，一场洪水、一笔债和一场久病都能叫 miseries。

abstract.en: Calling a complainer a misery suggests that sorrow can spread from one person into a whole room.
abstract.cn: 把一个抱怨者叫作 misery，说明悲伤能从一个人扩散到整个房间。

examples.en: Years of misery had worn the family down before help arrived.
examples.cn: 在援助到来之前，多年的苦难已经把这一家人拖垮了。

examples.en: The flood brought misery to hundreds of villages.
examples.cn: 那场洪水给数百个村庄带来了苦难。

examples.en: Don't be such a misery and come to the party.
examples.cn: 别这么爱抱怨了，来参加聚会吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米泽瑞」——米不够、灯又快灭，日子就苦；记住 misery 是痛苦、苦难。

root: 拉丁语 miser（不幸的人）派生 miseria（悲惨、苦难），经古法语 misere 进入英语；与 miserable、commiserate 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stuck state of wretchedness; the senses divide into the lasting feeling, the events that cause it, and the person who spreads it through complaint.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种无法摆脱的悲惨处境；义项分为持续的感受、造成感受的事件，以及靠抱怨把这种状态扩散开来的人。

branches.cn: 蜷在冷屋子角落里的人

branches.en: a flood taking away what a family had
branches.cn: 洪水冲走一个家庭原有的东西

branches.en: a debt that grows while a wage stays small
branches.cn: 工资不涨而债越滚越大

branches.en: a voice complaining through a whole meal
branches.cn: 一顿饭里抱怨不停的声音

branches.en: one gloomy guest darkening a bright room
branches.cn: 一个阴郁的客人让明亮的房间暗下来

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin noun for wretchedness, the adjective behind it, the verb of pity, the French form and the English plural.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词、它背后的形容词、表示怜悯的动词、法语形式以及英语复数共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Misery comes from a Latin noun of wretchedness built on miser, so the Latin side records the noun, the adjective and the verb of pity.
latinIntro.cn: misery 来自建立在 miser 上、表示悲惨处境的拉丁语名词，因此拉丁同源部分记录名词、形容词与表示怜悯的动词。

definition_zh: 误导；使误解；带错路；使产生错误印象
definition_en: to cause someone to believe something that is not true; to guide a person along the wrong way; and of a thing, to give a false impression
core_image: 路口一块指向反方向的木牌，行人照着箭头走进雾里
scene: 山路口立着一块被人转反的木牌，几个行人照着箭头走进雾里，越走越偏。A single confusing sign can mislead even an experienced driver.
sceneCN: 这里是「带错路」（第 2 个义项：指错方向）；句意为一块让人困惑的路牌，即使经验丰富的司机也会被带错方向。图中可辨识物件：转反的木牌、雾、走进雾里的行人。

pos.zh: 误导；使误解；带错路；使产生错误印象

derivatives.zh: 由 mislead 加 -ing 构成，义为「误导性的；引入歧途的」
由 misleading 加 -ly 构成，义为「以误导的方式」

senses.title: To cause someone to believe something false
senses.definition: to make someone accept an untrue idea, often without any deliberate intention to lie
senses.definitionCN: 使某人把不真实的想法当成真的，常常并非有意撒谎
senses.example: The advertisement misleads buyers about the true cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告在真实花费上误导了买家。
senses.why: Mis- marks a wrong turn and lead is the act of guiding, so mislead is guidance that ends in a false belief rather than in a false place.
senses.whyCN: mis- 标出一个错误的方向，lead 是引领的动作，所以 mislead 是把人引向错误信念的引导，而不只是把路带错。

senses.title: To guide someone along the wrong way
senses.definition: to lead a person or group along a wrong route, or away from the place they meant to reach
senses.definitionCN: 把人或一群人带到错误的路线，或带离他们原本要去的地方
senses.example: The old map misled us into a dead-end valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那张旧地图把我们带进了一条没有出口的山谷。
senses.why: Before it described deceiving the mind, the word described taking someone by the hand and walking them the wrong way, and that physical sense still survives beside the mental one.
senses.whyCN: 在用来描述蒙蔽头脑之前，这个词说的是牵着人走错路；这一身体层面的意思至今仍与头脑层面的意思并存。

senses.title: To give a false impression of something
senses.definition: of an appearance, a result or a piece of evidence, to suggest something that is not actually the case
senses.definitionCN: 指外表、结果或证据让人以为某事成立，而事实并非如此
senses.example: The first results misled the researchers into expecting a quick cure.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的结果让研究人员误以为很快就能找到疗法。
senses.why: If a person can be led astray, so can an observer's judgement; the word then describes evidence that pulls the mind down a wrong path without anyone telling a lie.
senses.whyCN: 既然人能被人带偏，观察者的判断也能被带偏；于是这个词描述的是把头脑拽上错误路径的证据，即使没有谁说谎。

intro.en: Mislead is an Old English compound of mis-, meaning wrong, and lædan, to lead; its past tense misled still hides an irregular vowel change.
intro.cn: mislead 是古英语中用 mis-（错误）与 lædan（引领）构成的复合词；它的过去式 misled 仍保留着不规则的元音变化。

items.en: The prefix mis- meant wrong, badly or astray, and it was freely added to English verbs.
items.cn: 前缀 mis- 意为错误、不当、走偏，可以自由地加在英语动词前面。

items.en: Lædan meant to lead or to bring a person along a way, and it is the verb behind modern lead.
items.cn: lædan 意为引领、把人带在路上走，是现代 lead 背后的动词。

items.en: Mislædan joined the two parts and meant to lead astray, first in the literal sense of a wrong road.
items.cn: mislædan 把两部分组合起来，意为引人入歧途，最初是字面意义上的走错路。

items.en: Middle English kept the literal sense and began to use the word for leading someone's mind into error.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了字面义，并开始用这个词表示把人的想法引入错误。

items.en: Modern English uses mislead mostly for false beliefs and false impressions, while the wrong-road sense stays in the background.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 mislead 表示错误信念与错误印象，而「带错路」的意思退到了背景里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and relatives of mislead plus one word built on the same prefix; the near-meaning group collects verbs for guiding someone into error.
note.cn: 形近组收 mislead 的各种形式与同族词，外加一个用同一前缀构成的词；近义组收表示把人引向错误的动词。

entries.definition: Giving a false impression; the present participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 给人错误印象的；现在分词用作形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of mislead.
entries.definitionCN: mislead 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: In a way that gives a false impression.
entries.definitionCN: 以给人错误印象的方式。

entries.definition: To give someone wrong information; it shares the prefix mis- but uses inform.
entries.definitionCN: 向某人提供错误信息；共用前缀 mis-，但词干是 inform。

entries.definition: To make someone believe something false, usually on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人相信不真实的事，通常是有意的。

entries.definition: To make someone do or believe something by a clever ruse.
entries.definitionCN: 用巧妙的手段让人做某事或相信某事。

entries.definition: To guide someone badly or along a wrong course.
entries.definitionCN: 把人带坏或引向错误方向。

entries.definition: To send someone or something in the wrong direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物送往错误的方向。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of a Germanic prefix for wrongness and the verb to lead; its family keeps returning to guidance that ends somewhere nobody meant to go.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示错误的日耳曼语前缀与动词「引领」构成，同族词反复回到通向谁都不想去之处的引导。

normal.en: Mislead is made of mis-, wrong, and lead, to guide, so the word pictures guidance that ends in error.
normal.cn: mislead 由 mis-（错误）与 lead（引领）构成，所以这个词画出的是以错误收场的引导。

normal.en: Lead is an Old English verb, which is why the past tense is misled and not misleaded.
normal.cn: lead 是古英语动词，所以过去式是 misled，而不是 misleaded。

normal.en: Misled looks like a different word but is simply the past form, made by changing the vowel rather than adding -ed.
normal.cn: misled 看起来像另一个词，其实只是过去式，靠换元音而不是加 -ed 构成。

normal.en: Misleading keeps the same idea for things rather than people: a sign, a result or a statistic can lead the mind astray.
normal.cn: misleading 把同样的意思用在物而不是人身上：路牌、结果或统计数据都能把头脑带偏。

normal.en: Misinform shares the prefix mis- but uses inform instead of lead, so the two words describe error delivered as news and error delivered as guidance.
normal.cn: misinform 共用前缀 mis-，但词干是 inform 而不是 lead，于是两个词分别描述以消息形式送来的错误和以引导形式送来的错误。

abstract.en: A reversed signpost is the whole story: nobody lied to the traveller, yet the road still ends in the wrong place.
abstract.cn: 一块转反的路牌就是全部故事：没有谁对旅人说谎，路却仍然通向错误的地方。

abstract.en: The word keeps body and mind in one frame, since a wrong road and a false belief are both reached by following someone.
abstract.cn: 这个词把身体与头脑放在同一幅画里，因为走错的路与信错的念头都是跟着别人走到的。

abstract.en: Because mislead often needs no intention to lie, it can describe a result as easily as it describes a liar.
abstract.cn: 因为 mislead 常常不需要撒谎的意图，它既能形容一个骗子，也能同样轻松地形容一个结果。

examples.en: The advertisement misleads buyers about the true cost.
examples.cn: 这则广告在真实花费上误导了买家。

examples.en: The old map misled us into a dead-end valley.
examples.cn: 那张旧地图把我们带进了一条没有出口的山谷。

examples.en: The first results misled the researchers into expecting a quick cure.
examples.cn: 最初的结果让研究人员误以为很快就能找到疗法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米斯立德」——米斯把人领到一条错路上；记住 mislead 是误导、带错路。

root: 古英语 mis-（错误）加 lædan（引领）构成 mislædan，意为「带错路」，后引申为「把人的想法引向错误」；lead 属于日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is guidance that ends in error; the senses divide into a false belief, a literal wrong route, and evidence that gives a false impression.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是通向错误的引导；义项分为错误信念、字面意义上的错路，以及造成错误印象的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signpost turned the wrong way, walkers following its arrow into the fog and drifting further off.
core.cn: 核心意象：路口一块指向反方向的木牌，行人照着箭头走进雾里，越走越偏。

branches.en: a walker following a reversed sign into fog
branches.cn: 跟着转反的路牌走进雾里的行人

branches.en: a buyer trusting a price that hides its extras
branches.cn: 买家相信一个藏了附加费的价格

branches.en: a first result pointing at a cure that is not there
branches.cn: 最初结果指向一个并不存在的疗法

branches.en: a hand on the shoulder steering someone off the path
branches.cn: 搭在肩上的手把人引离小路

branches.en: a compass and a chart both pointing wrong
branches.cn: 指南针与海图都指错了方向

intro.en: The word is carried by the Germanic prefix for wrongness, the Old English verb to lead, its modern form and the endings that build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示错误的日耳曼语前缀、古英语中表示引领的动词、它的现代形式，以及构成形容词与副词的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mislead: both mis- and lead belong to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: mislead 没有可靠的拉丁同族词：mis- 与 lead 都属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

items.meaning: to guide, to show the way

definition_zh: 错过；未击中；想念；察觉缺失；（Miss）小姐
definition_en: to fail to hit, catch, reach or attend something, to feel sad because someone is absent, and, as a separate title, to address an unmarried woman
core_image: 一支箭擦着靶边飞过，靶心还空着
scene: 站台上人群已经跑得气喘，铁门却在眼前合拢。We sprinted for the platform, but the doors closed and we missed the evening train.
sceneCN: 这里是「错过车次」（第 2 个义项：太晚而失去班次）；句意为两人冲向站台，门已关上，错过了晚间那班车。图中可辨识物件：站台铁门、奔跑的人群、末班车的灯光。

pos.zh: 错过；未击中；想念；察觉缺失

derivatives.zh: 由 miss 加 -ing 构成，指不在原处、缺失或失踪的
由过去分词转作形容词，指被错过、未能抓住的
由 miss 加 -able 构成，指可以略过、不值得一看的

senses.title: To fail to hit or catch a target
senses.definition: to aim at something and fail to touch it, catch it or land on it
senses.definitionCN: 瞄准某物却没能碰到、接住或落在上面
senses.example: He swung at the ball but missed it completely.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝球挥棒，却完全没打中。
senses.why: Old English missan described a shot or a blow that went wide of its mark, and that physical failure to connect is the picture every later sense keeps borrowing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 missan 最早说的是一箭或一击偏了靶心、没能碰上目标；这种身体上「没接上」的画面，是后面每个义项一直在借用的起点。

senses.title: To be too late for a train, bus or chance
senses.definition: to arrive too late for a bus, train or opportunity, so that it is lost
senses.definitionCN: 到达得太晚，没能赶上公交、火车或机会，于是失去它
senses.example: We ran for the platform but missed the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们朝站台跑过去，却错过了最后一班火车。
senses.why: A train leaves on its own timetable, so missing it repeats the same failure to connect, now measured in minutes rather than in inches.
senses.whyCN: 列车按自己的时刻表开走，「错过」还是那次没接上，只是衡量的尺度从几寸变成了几分钟，于是同一个词从靶场挪到了站台。

senses.title: To feel sad because someone is absent
senses.definition: to feel unhappy because a person or thing you care about is not with you
senses.definitionCN: 因为牵挂的人或物不在身边而感到难过
senses.example: She missed her family more than she had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 她想念家人的程度超出了自己的预料。
senses.why: Since missan could also mean to be without something, the verb could name the ache of that absence; the target you fail to reach becomes a person you fail to keep near.
senses.whyCN: 既然 missan 还能表示「身边没有某物」，这个词就可以指那份缺席带来的空落；没能击中的目标，变成了没能守在身边的人。

senses.title: To notice that something is not there
senses.definition: to notice that a thing or person is no longer in its usual place
senses.definitionCN: 察觉到某物或某人已不在原来的位置
senses.example: I missed my wallet only when I reached the till.
senses.exampleCN: 直到走到收银台，我才发现钱包不见了。
senses.why: A hand still reaches for the pocket where the wallet always sits, and the empty place is what the eye reports; the sense turns absence into a small act of noticing.
senses.whyCN: 手仍按老习惯伸向总放钱包的口袋，眼睛报告的是那块空处；这一层把「缺少」变成了一个察觉的动作。

senses.title: A title for an unmarried woman
senses.definition: a title placed before the surname of an unmarried woman, or used in direct address
senses.definitionCN: 放在未婚女子姓氏之前、或用于当面称呼的称谓
senses.example: Miss Adams teaches the youngest class.
senses.exampleCN: 亚当斯小姐教年纪最小的那个班。
senses.why: This title is a different word altogether, a shortened form of mistress, which once meant a woman in charge; as mistress narrowed, the clipped form kept only the neutral address, which is why it merely looks like the verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓其实是另一个词：mistress 的缩略，本指「掌家的女人」；后来 mistress 词义收窄，缩略形式只留下中性的称呼，所以它只是碰巧和动词长得一样。

intro.en: Miss is a Germanic verb for going wide of a mark; it reached English before the Norman conquest, and a separate word later shrank into the title Miss.
intro.cn: miss 是日耳曼语中表示「偏出目标」的动词，在诺曼征服之前就进入英语；另有一个与它无关的词后来缩略成了称谓 Miss。

items.en: The reconstructed form *missijan- meant to go wrong or to fail to reach, and it is the common ancestor of the Germanic verbs of missing.
items.cn: *missijan- 是重构形式，意为「走岔、没能到达」，是日耳曼语各语支里「错过」类动词的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English missan meant to fail to hit or reach something, and it could also mean to be without it.
items.cn: 古英语 missan 意为没能击中或到达某物，也可以指身边没有它。

items.en: Middle English kept both strands alive: failing to hit a target and lacking something that ought to be there.
items.cn: 中古英语把两条线都留着：既指没打中目标，也指缺了本该有的东西。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb was used for feeling a person's absence, while the noun a miss named a shot that went wide.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已经用来表示感到某人不在身边；名词 a miss 则指打偏的一击。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb for targets, timetables and absent people; the title Miss is a shortening of mistress, a different word that merely looks the same.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个动词负责目标、时刻表与缺席的人；称谓 Miss 是 mistress 的缩略，来历不同，只是碰巧长得一样。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived form and the shared mis- prefix, including a word that only borrows the prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of losing, skipping and failing to notice.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与共用的 mis- 前缀，也包括只借了前缀的词；近义组收表示失去、跳过与没留意的动词。

entries.definition: The present participle of miss used as an adjective: not in the expected place.
entries.definitionCN: miss 的现在分词转作形容词，指不在原处；缺失的。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning wrongly or badly, the same sideways idea that lives inside miss.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地、不当」的前缀，和 miss 里那股「偏了」的意味一脉相承。

entries.definition: A wrong act or judgement; it uses mis- but its stem comes from Norse taka, so it is no relative of miss.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的行为或判断；它用了 mis- 前缀，但词干来自北欧语的 taka，与 miss 并非同族。

entries.definition: To spell a word wrongly; built from mis- and spell, with no link to the verb beyond the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 把单词拼错；由 mis- 加 spell 构成，除前缀外与动词 miss 没有关系。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, often because it slips away.
entries.definitionCN: 不再拥有某物，常因它溜走而失去。

entries.definition: To leave something out or stay away from it on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意略过某事或不去参加。

entries.definition: To fail to notice something that is there in plain view.
entries.definitionCN: 没能注意到就摆在眼前的东西。

entries.definition: To want someone or something very much, especially someone who is absent.
entries.definitionCN: 非常渴望某人或某物，尤指不在身边的人。

normalIntro.en: The verb began as an arrow going wide of its mark, and the whole family keeps that sideways step in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词从一支偏出靶心的箭开始，整个词族始终盯着那一步「偏到一边」。

normal.en: Old English missan already meant to go wide of a mark, so every sense begins with a shot that does not land.
normal.cn: 古英语 missan 本就说「偏了靶心」，所以每个义项都从一支没落地的箭开始。

normal.en: The prefix mis- carries the same sideways idea, which is why mistake and misspell both describe a step to the wrong side.
normal.cn: 前缀 mis- 带着同样的「偏到一边」的意味，所以 mistake 与 misspell 都描述走错一步。

normal.en: Miss the bus keeps the archery picture alive: the bus was the mark, and you arrived after it moved.
normal.cn: miss the bus 把射箭的画面留着：车就是靶，你到的时候它已经走了。

normal.en: Missing adds -ing and turns the failure into a state: what is missing is simply not where it belongs.
normal.cn: missing 加 -ing，把「没打中」变成一种状态：missing 的东西就是不在它该在的地方。

normal.en: The title Miss is a clipped mistress, a completely separate word, so it carries no sense of failing to hit anything.
normal.cn: 称谓 Miss 是 mistress 的缩略，完全是另一个词，所以它跟「没打中」毫无关系。

abstract.en: A word that starts with an arrow in the air ends up naming the ache of an empty room, which shows how far one failure can travel.
abstract.cn: 一个从空中飞箭开始的词，最后指称空房间里的那种酸楚，说明一次「没碰上」能走多远。

abstract.en: Missing a train and missing a person both leave a gap where something should have been.
abstract.cn: 错过一班车和想念一个人，都在本该有东西的位置留下空白。

abstract.en: The title sitting beside the verb is a reminder that identical shapes can hide unrelated histories.
abstract.cn: 同一个拼写旁边站着动词和称谓，提醒人：相同的形状可以藏着毫不相干的来历。

examples.en: He reached for the ball and missed it by a finger.
examples.cn: 他伸手去接球，只差一指没接住。

examples.en: I missed the early bus and walked to school.
examples.cn: 我错过了早班车，只好走去学校。

examples.en: She missed her brother most on quiet evenings.
examples.cn: 安静的傍晚，她最想念哥哥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「觅思」——想「觅」却只能「思」，正是错过与想念的滋味。

root: 古英语 missan（没击中、没到达），属日耳曼语族，更早为重构形式 *missijan-（走岔）；与拉丁语 mittere 并非同源，只是形近。称谓 Miss 另出 mistress 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The physical failure to hit comes first; the senses then move to a timetable, to a person who is absent, to a gap noticed in a pocket, and finally to a title that merely shares the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是身体上没击中；义项接着走向时刻表、走向不在身边的人、走向口袋里的空处，最后走向一个只是碰巧同形的称谓。

core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭擦着靶边飞过，靶心还空着。

branches.cn: 球棒挥过球旁，只扫到空气

branches.en: a platform gate closing just before a late runner
branches.cn: 站台门在迟到者面前合拢

branches.en: an empty chair kept for someone far away
branches.cn: 为远方的人留着的一把空椅

branches.cn: 手拍向本该放钱包的口袋

branches.cn: 教室门上写着一个姓氏

intro.en: The word rests on an Old English verb of going wide, the prefix mis-, and a set of English endings that build new forms and relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词靠一个表示「偏出」的古英语动词、前缀 mis-，以及一组造出新形式与同族词的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for miss; the word belongs to the Germanic branch, and the similar-looking Latin mittere is a false friend.
latinIntro.cn: miss 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它属于日耳曼语这一支，形似的拉丁语 mittere 只是一个假朋友。

items.meaning: to fail to hit, to go wrong

definition_zh: 导弹；投掷物；弹丸
definition_en: a weapon that flies through the air to hit a distant target, or, in older use, any object thrown or fired
core_image: 一道白线划破天空，拐了个弯追向远处的靶
scene: 试验场的雷达屏幕亮着，远处拖出一道白线。Operators watched the missile bank in mid-air and follow the target drone across the sky.
sceneCN: 这里是「导弹」（第 1 个义项：可制导的远程武器）；句意为操作员看着导弹在空中转弯，追着靶机划过天空。图中可辨识物件：雷达屏幕、白线、靶机。

derivatives.zh: 由 missile 加表示「人」的 -eer 构成，指从事导弹工作或操作导弹的人
由 missile 加 -ry 构成，指导弹的总称或导弹技术
由 anti-（反）与 missile 复合而成，指用于拦截导弹的

senses.title: A guided weapon that flies to a distant target
senses.definition: a weapon, usually rocket-powered, that is launched and then guided through the air to hit a distant target
senses.definitionCN: 一种通常由火箭推进的武器，发射后可被引导飞向远处目标
senses.example: The defence system tracked the incoming missile from the moment it left the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 防御系统从导弹离地那一刻起就跟踪着它。
senses.why: Latin missile first meant any object thrown; once engineers could steer that object while it flew, the old word for a thrown thing took on the modern sense of a guided weapon.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 missile 本指任何被投出的东西；当工程师能让飞行中的物体改变方向，这个「投出去的东西」就顺势成了能被引导的现代武器。

senses.title: An object thrown by hand as a weapon
senses.definition: a stone, spear or other object thrown by hand to strike someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 用手投出去、用来击打人或物的石头、长矛等物体
senses.example: The crowd threw stones and other missiles at the soldiers.
senses.exampleCN: 人群朝士兵投掷石块和其他投掷物。
senses.why: Before engines existed, the only way to send a blow across a distance was to throw something, and the Latin noun named exactly that object in the air.
senses.whyCN: 在有发动机之前，要把打击送到远处，只能靠手把东西扔出去；拉丁语名词指的正是空中那件被投出的物体，这是最贴近字面的一层。

senses.title: A projectile fired from a gun or cannon
senses.definition: a shell, bullet or similar projectile fired from a gun or cannon rather than thrown by hand
senses.definitionCN: 由枪炮射出而非用手投出的炮弹、子弹之类
senses.example: Old gunnery manuals list the weight of every missile the battery could fire.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的火炮手册会列出炮组能射出的每一种弹丸的重量。
senses.why: Gunpowder replaced the arm but not the idea: the object still leaves a hand or a barrel and flies to a target, so the same word stretched from stones to shells.
senses.whyCN: 火药换了手臂的位置，却换不掉那个念头：物体仍要从手里或炮口飞向目标，于是同一个词从石头一路盖到了炮弹。

intro.en: Missile comes straight from Latin, where it named any object thrown; English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century and later applied it to self-propelled weapons.
intro.cn: missile 直接来自拉丁语，本指任何被投出的物体；英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，后来才用它指自推进的武器。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, let go or throw, and its supine missum supplied the stem for a whole family of sending words.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放开、投掷，它的动名词形式 missum 为整整一族「送」的词提供了词干。

items.en: The adjective missilis meant that may be thrown, formed from the same stem with the suffix -ilis.
items.cn: 形容词 missilis 意为「可以被投出的」，由同一词干加后缀 -ilis 构成。

items.en: The neuter noun missile meant a thing thrown, whether a stone, a spear or a bolt.
items.cn: 中性名词 missile 指被投出的东西，可以是石头、长矛或弩箭。

items.en: English took the Latin noun in the seventeenth century, first for thrown objects and later for projectiles fired from guns.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入这个拉丁名词，先指被投掷的物体，后来也指枪炮射出的弹丸。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word narrowed onto rocket-powered weapons that steer in flight, while the older sense survives in historical writing.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词收窄到指飞行中可自行导向的火箭武器，较旧的含义则留在历史叙述里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Latin relatives and one derived person noun; the near-meaning group gathers flying weapons and the parts or payloads that travel with them.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁同族词与一个派生的人物名词；近义组收飞行武器以及随它一起飞行的部件或载荷。

entries.definition: The Latin adjective meaning able to be thrown, the direct source of missile.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语形容词，意为「可以被投出的」，正是 missile 的直接来源。

entries.definition: A task or a sending out, formed from the same Latin verb mittere.
entries.definitionCN: 任务或一次派遣，来自同一个拉丁动词 mittere。

entries.definition: To send someone away, built from dis- plus mittere.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人打发走，由 dis- 加 mittere 构成。

entries.definition: A person who works with or operates missiles.
entries.definitionCN: 从事导弹工作或操作导弹的人。

entries.definition: A vehicle driven by burning fuel and used to carry a warhead or a spacecraft.
entries.definitionCN: 靠燃烧燃料推进的飞行器，用来运送弹头或航天器。

entries.definition: Any object moving through the air after being thrown or fired.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被抛出或射出后在空中飞行的物体。

entries.definition: A self-propelled weapon that travels underwater toward a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 一种在水下自行推进、冲向舰船的武器。

entries.definition: The part of a missile that carries the explosive or the payload.
entries.definitionCN: 导弹中装载炸药或有效载荷的部分。

normalIntro.en: Latin mittere meant to send, and every relative of this word is about something or someone being sent.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送出」，这个词的同族词都在说某物或某人被送出去。

normal.en: Mittere meant to send, and missile is literally the thing sent.
normal.cn: mittere 意为「送出」，missile 字面就是「被送出的东西」。

normal.en: Missilis was the adjective for throwable, so the noun began in the air as a stone or a spear, not in a silo.
normal.cn: missilis 是「可投掷的」形容词，所以这个名词最早是在空中的石头或长矛，而不是在发射井里。

normal.en: Mission and dismiss share the same verb, one a sending out and one a sending away.
normal.cn: mission 与 dismiss 共用同一个动词，一个是派出去，一个是打发走。

normal.en: The modern weapon keeps the old grammar: something is still sent toward a target, only now it can steer.
normal.cn: 现代武器沿用旧的语法：仍有东西被送向目标，只是现在它能自己转向。

normal.en: Warhead, booster and guidance describe parts, while missile itself claims only that the object is thrown.
normal.cn: 弹头、助推器与制导描述的是零件，而 missile 本身只声明「这个物体是被投出去的」。

abstract.en: Every missile is a sentence in the oldest grammar of distance: I send this toward you.
abstract.cn: 每一枚导弹都在用最古老的「距离语法」说话：我把这个送向你。

abstract.en: The word stayed the same while the thrower changed from an arm to a rocket, which is how language survives technology.
abstract.cn: 投掷者从手臂换成火箭，词却没有变，语言就是这样熬过技术的更替。

abstract.en: A weapon named for throwing reminds us that the noun describes motion, not moral weight.
abstract.cn: 一个以「投掷」命名的武器提醒人：这个词描述的是运动，不是道德重量。

examples.en: The missile climbed steeply and then levelled off toward the coast.
examples.cn: 导弹陡直爬升，随后改平飞向海岸。

examples.en: A single missile can carry several warheads.
examples.cn: 一枚导弹可以携带多个弹头。

examples.en: The old manual still called a stone a missile.
examples.cn: 那本旧手册仍把石头称作投掷物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米赛尔」——像一支点火的箭在赛跑，一路冲向远方目标。

root: 拉丁语 mittere（送出、投掷）的词干 miss- 加形容词后缀 -ilis 得 missilis（可投掷的），其中性名词 missile 指「被投出之物」；十七世纪进入英语，二十世纪专指可制导的导弹。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is a modern guided weapon; the other two keep the older meaning of any object sent through the air, whether by hand or by gunpowder.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项是现代的可制导武器；另外两个保留较旧的含义——任何被送过空中的物体，无论靠手还是靠火药。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white trail bending across the sky toward a far target.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道白线划破天空，拐了个弯追向远处的靶。

branches.en: a white trail bending in the sky toward a drone
branches.cn: 天空里一道转弯的白线追向靶机

branches.en: a stone leaving a hand and finding a shield
branches.cn: 石头离开手，撞上盾牌

branches.en: a cannon barrel flashing above a fortress wall
branches.cn: 炮口在城墙上方一闪

branches.en: a word for a thrown thing surviving into the rocket age
branches.cn: 「投出之物」的说法一路活到火箭时代

branches.en: one crew counting shells and another counting rockets
branches.cn: 一班人数炮弹，另一班人数火箭

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of sending, built from a verb, its supine stem and an adjective suffix, plus English relatives that kept the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「送」的名词，由一个动词、它的动名词词干和一个形容词后缀构成，再加上沿用同一词干的英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere and its supine missum are the direct source, and the Latin adjective missilis supplies the ending -ilis that marks something as throwable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 及其动名词 missum 是直接来源，拉丁形容词 missilis 则提供了表示「可以被投掷」的后缀 -ilis。

items.meaning: a weapon that flies to a target

definition_zh: 使命；任务；（派往国外的）代表团；传教工作；飞行或军事任务
definition_en: a task that a person or group is sent to carry out, or the purpose an organization sets for itself
core_image: 一个人把封好的信交到另一个人手里，那人转身就上路
scene: 山里的诊所缺药，一支小队带着箱子走了两天，把药送到村口就返回。The team's mission was to reach the village before the rains.
sceneCN: 这里 mission 指被派出去要完成的一项具体任务（第 1 个义项：受派执行的任务）；句意：这支小队的任务是赶在雨季前抵达那个村子。图中可辨识物件：药箱、山路、封好的指令、雨云；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 使命；任务；代表团；传教；飞行任务

derivatives.zh: 传教士；传教的
使命宣言
任务控制中心
委员会；委托
解散；解雇

senses.title: An organization's declared purpose
senses.titleCN: 一个组织公开宣告的宗旨
senses.definition: the purpose that an organization states as its reason for existing
senses.definitionCN: 一个组织声明为其存在理由的宗旨
senses.example: The mission on the clinic wall is one sentence long.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所墙上的宗旨只有一句话。
senses.why: A body that is sent must know what it was sent for, so the word came to mean a declared purpose.
senses.whyCN: 被派出去的团体必须知道自己为何被派，这个词于是也指公开宣告的宗旨。

senses.title: A journey with a set purpose
senses.titleCN: 带有明确目的的一次出行
senses.definition: a journey or trip undertaken to carry out a particular task
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某项特定任务而进行的行程
senses.example: The supply mission took two days over the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 那次补给任务翻过山口用了两天。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a sending: someone is dispatched, and the going is the task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「被派出」：有人被派遣出去，走这一趟就是任务。

senses.title: A group sent abroad
senses.definition: a group of officials sent to another country to represent their government
senses.definitionCN: 被派往他国代表本国政府的官员团体
senses.example: The trade mission met three buyers in one week.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易代表团一周内见了三位买家。
senses.why: When the sending is diplomatic, the word names the people who were sent rather than the errand.
senses.whyCN: 当派遣是外交性质时，这个词指被派出去的人，而不是那件差事。

senses.title: Religious work or a station
senses.definition: the work of spreading a faith, or the settlement where that work is based
senses.definitionCN: 传播信仰的工作，或这项工作所在的驻地
senses.example: The mission ran a school and a small hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那个传教站办了一所学校和一间小医院。
senses.why: Missionaries were sent, so their posting took the name of the sending.
senses.whyCN: 传教士是被派出去的，因此他们的驻地沿用了「派遣」这个名字。

senses.title: A military operation with an objective
senses.titleCN: 有明确目标的军事行动
senses.definition: a single operation with a stated objective, often by aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 一次有既定目标的行动，常指飞机出动
senses.example: The squadron flew nine missions in a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个中队一个月里飞了九次任务。
senses.why: An aircrew is sent out with an objective, and the flight becomes the mission.
senses.whyCN: 机组带着目标被派出，这次飞行就成了 mission。

senses.title: A personal calling
senses.definition: the duty that a person feels bound to fulfil in life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人觉得自己一生必须完成的职责
senses.example: Her mission was to teach girls in villages to read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的使命是教村里的女孩识字。
senses.why: A sending can come from inside rather than from a sender, and the word then means a calling.
senses.whyCN: 派遣也可以来自内心而不是来自派遣者，这个词于是指一种召唤。

senses.title: An embassy or delegation office
senses.titleCN: 使馆或代表处的办公机构
senses.definition: the office or building of a country's representative abroad
senses.definitionCN: 一国驻外代表所在的办公机构或馆舍
senses.example: The visa section is on the second floor of the mission.
senses.exampleCN: 签证处在代表处的二楼。
senses.why: The people sent need a place to work, and the building takes the name of the group.
senses.whyCN: 被派出去的人需要一个办公的地方，馆舍便沿用了这群人的名称。

senses.title: A task given to one person
senses.titleCN: 交给某一个人的具体差事
senses.definition: a particular errand or job assigned to an individual
senses.definitionCN: 分配给某一个人的具体差事
senses.example: His mission for the afternoon was to find the missing file.
senses.exampleCN: 他下午的差事是把那份不见的档案找出来。
senses.why: The word scales down to one person and one errand, keeping the same shape of being sent.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能缩小到一个人、一件差事，仍然保持「被派出」的形状。

intro.en: Mission comes from Latin missio 'a sending', built on mittere 'to send'. English first used it for the sending of envoys and missionaries, and later for any task someone is sent to do.
intro.cn: mission 来自拉丁 missio「派遣」，由 mittere「发送」构成。英语最初用它指派遣使节与传教士，后来才指任何被派去完成的任务。

items.en: Latin mittere 'to send, let go' is well recorded, but its deeper origin is uncertain and no older root can be stated with confidence.
items.cn: 拉丁 mittere「发送、放出」记录充分，但其更早来源不确定，无法有把握地给出更古老的词根。

items.en: The past participle missus 'sent' supplies the miss- inside mission, missionary and missile.
items.cn: 过去分词 missus「被送出的」提供了 mission、missionary 与 missile 里的 miss-。

items.en: Missio meant a sending or a letting go; in military Latin it could also mean a discharge from service.
items.cn: missio 意为派遣或放行；在军事拉丁语里也可指解除兵役。

items.en: English took mission in the sixteenth century, first for the sending of envoys, then for the sending of missionaries.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 mission，先指派遣使节，再指派遣传教士。

items.en: By the seventeenth century a mission could be the station itself, and by the eighteenth a permanent embassy.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，mission 可指传教站本身；到十八世纪，又可指常设使馆。

items.en: Aviation, space flight and management gave the word its operation and purpose senses in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 航空、航天与管理在二十世纪赋予这个词「行动」与「宗旨」两义。

note.en: The first group shares the miss- root; the second group names other tasks and purposes.
note.cn: 第一组共享 miss- 词根；第二组是其他任务与宗旨的说法。

entries.definition: From missus 'sent', but it names a weapon that is thrown or fired, not a task.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 missus「被送出的」，但指被投出或发射的武器，不是任务。

entries.definition: From dis- 'away' plus mittere 'send', meaning to send away or let go.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dis-「离开」加 mittere「发送」构成，意为打发走、解散。

entries.definition: From trans- 'across' plus mittere, meaning to send across.
entries.definitionCN: 由 trans-「越过」加 mittere 构成，意为发送过去。

entries.definition: From com- 'together' plus mittere, meaning to entrust a task or the body entrusted with it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 mittere 构成，意为委托任务，或指受托的机构。

entries.definition: A piece of work to be done, with no idea of being sent.
entries.definitionCN: 一件要做的工作，不含「被派出」之意。

entries.definition: Work given to a person by someone in authority; it stresses the giving.
entries.definitionCN: 由有权者交给某人的工作，强调交付。

entries.definition: The aim behind an action, which is the first sense of mission within an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 行动背后的目标，正是 mission 在组织内部的第一义。

entries.definition: A group sent with authority to represent others, close to the diplomatic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 受权代表他人而被派出的团体，接近外交义。

entries.definition: A strong sense of being called to a kind of work, close to the personal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈感到被召唤去做某类工作，接近个人天职义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Mittere is to send, and missio is a sending, so a mission is literally something sent.
normal.cn: mittere 是发送，missio 是派遣，因此 mission 字面上就是「被派出的事」。

normal.en: The family runs mission, missionary, missile, dismiss and transmit.
normal.cn: 同族词有 missionary、missile、dismiss 与 transmit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: mission statement, rescue mission, space mission.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出它的用法：使命宣言、救援任务、太空飞行任务。

normal.en: The same word scales from a whole organisation's purpose down to one afternoon errand.
normal.cn: 同一个词能从整个组织的宗旨缩小到一个下午的差事。

normal.en: A sending needs a sender, a message and a road, which is the whole picture.
normal.cn: 一次派遣需要派遣者、消息与一条路，这就是整幅画面。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed letter handed over and a traveller turning at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一封封好的信被交出，旅人当场转身。

abstract.en: Picture a box carried two days over a pass, never set down.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「miss（送出）+ ion（名词）」——被送出去要做的事，就是任务

root: 拉丁 mittere「发送」→ 过去分词 missus「被送出的」→ missio「派遣」→ 英语 mission。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with a sending: an organization's declared purpose, a purposeful journey, a group sent abroad, a mission station, a military sortie, a personal calling, an embassy office and one person's errand.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一次派遣开始：组织宣告的宗旨、有目的的出行、派往国外的团体、传教站、军事出动、个人天职、使馆馆舍，以及一个人的差事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter handed over, and a traveller who turns and leaves at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封封好的信被交出，旅人转身立刻出发。

branches.en: WHY AND BY WHOM: a declared purpose, and a calling that feels like a sender inside.
branches.cn: 为何与由谁：公开宣告的宗旨，以及像内心派遣者一样的召唤。

branches.en: THE GOING ITSELF: a purposeful trip, and a sortie with a stated objective.
branches.cn: 出行本身：一趟有目的的行程，以及一次有既定目标的出动。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THEIR ROOM: a delegation abroad, and the building it works in.
branches.cn: 人与他们的房间：驻外代表团，以及它办公的馆舍。

branches.en: THE STATION: missionaries were sent, so their posting took the name of the sending.
branches.cn: 驻地：传教士被派出，因此驻地沿用了「派遣」之名。

branches.en: ONE ERRAND: the whole picture shrinks to a single afternoon's task.
branches.cn: 一件差事：整幅画面缩小到一个下午的任务。

intro.en: Mission is a Latin participle and action noun from the verb 'to send', and the same verb reaches several common English words.
intro.cn: mission 是由「发送」动词来的拉丁分词与动作名词，同一个动词还通向若干常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere gives mission, missile, dismiss, transmit and commission.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mittere 衍生 mission、missile（导弹）、dismiss（打发走）、transmit（传送）与 commission（委托）。
