definition_zh: 薄雾；水雾；朦胧；蒙上雾气
definition_en: a thin cloud of tiny water droplets near the ground, a fine spray in the air, a blur before the eyes, and the act of covering a surface with such droplets
core_image: 清晨的湖面浮着一层灰白色的薄纱，对岸的树看不清轮廓
scene: 湖面还没有亮起来，对岸的树只剩一层灰影。A thin mist hid the far shore until the sun rose.
sceneCN: 这里是「薄雾」（第 1 个义项：贴地的稀薄雾层）；句意为一层薄雾遮住远岸，直到太阳升起才散。图中可辨识物件：湖面、灰白的雾层、对岸的树影。

derivatives.zh: 由 mist 加 -y 构成，指有雾的、朦胧的
由 misty 加 -ly 构成，指朦胧地、雾蒙蒙地
由 misty 加 -ness 构成，指有雾、朦胧的状态

senses.title: Thin fog hanging close to the ground
senses.definition: a thin cloud of tiny water droplets near the ground that limits how far you can see
senses.definitionCN: 贴近地面、由细小水珠组成的稀薄雾层，会限制能见距离
senses.example: A cold mist covered the field before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 日出前，一层冷雾盖住了田野。
senses.why: Old English mist named the dimness itself, the grey that hides a distance; the droplets are the modern explanation of what produces that grey, not the starting point of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mist 先指的是「昏暗」本身，是那种把远处藏起来的灰；小水珠只是后人对这片灰的解释，并不是这个词的起点。

senses.title: A fine spray of liquid in the air
senses.definition: a cloud of very small droplets produced by spraying, splashing or cooling
senses.definitionCN: 由喷射、溅洒或冷却产生的细小水滴云
senses.example: A cool mist from the fountain settled on our faces.
senses.exampleCN: 喷泉送来的凉雾落在我们脸上。
senses.why: The same droplets can come from a nozzle or a wave instead of from cooling air; once the eye sees that cloud, the word follows it whatever produced it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的小水珠，可以来自喷头或浪花，而不一定来自空气冷却；眼睛只认那团悬浮的雾，于是词就跟着雾走，不管它是谁造的。

senses.title: A blur in front of the eyes or mind
senses.definition: a blur that keeps something from being seen clearly, especially one made by tears or strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 使某物看不清的一层模糊，尤指眼泪或强烈情绪造成的那种
senses.example: Tears rose and left her eyes in a mist.
senses.exampleCN: 泪水涌起，把她的眼睛蒙成一片朦胧。
senses.why: If mist can hide a field, it can hide anything the eye is trying to see; tears do to the eyes what weather does to a valley, so the word moves indoors.
senses.whyCN: 雾能把一片田野藏起来，就能把眼睛想看的一切藏起来；眼泪对眼睛做的事，正像天气对山谷做的事，于是这个词从户外挪进了眼眶。

senses.title: To cover or become covered with mist
senses.definition: to make a surface, especially glass, collect tiny droplets until it is hard to see through
senses.definitionCN: 使某表面（尤指玻璃）凝上细小水珠，以致看不透
senses.example: The bathroom mirror misted over after the hot shower.
senses.exampleCN: 热水澡之后，浴室的镜子蒙上了一层雾。
senses.why: When a surface collects the same droplets, the noun turns into a verb: the glass does not hold mist, it becomes misty, and English lets the noun carry that change.
senses.whyCN: 当表面凝上同样的小水珠，名词就顺手做了动词：玻璃不是「有雾」，而是「被雾蒙住」，英语让名词直接承担这个变化。

intro.en: Mist is an Old English word for dim air; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: mist 是古英语中表示「昏暗的空气」的词；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: The reconstructed form *mihstaz meant mist or dimness and is the common Germanic source of the word.
items.cn: *mihstaz 是重构形式，意为雾、昏暗，是这个词在日耳曼语中的共同来源。

items.en: Old English mist named dimness and hazy air, often carrying a sense of darkness as much as of weather.
items.cn: 古英语 mist 指昏暗与朦胧的空气，常常既指天气，也带着「暗」的意味。

items.en: Middle English mist kept the weather sense and began to appear in descriptions of landscape and sea.
items.cn: 中古英语的 mist 保留天气义，并开始出现在风景与海面的描写里。

items.en: Later writers extended the word to any fine cloud of droplets, including spray from water and smoke-like vapour.
items.cn: 后来的作者把词义扩展到任何细小的水珠云，包括水花溅起的雾和烟似的汽。

items.en: Modern English uses mist for thin ground fog, for fine spray, for a blur in the eye, and as a verb for a surface that fogs over.
items.cn: 现代英语用 mist 指贴地的薄雾、细小的水雾、眼前的朦胧，也作动词指表面蒙上雾气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and noun built on this stem plus one word that merely looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers other forms of suspended water and the words for heavier or lighter weather.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形容词与名词，外加一个只是形似的词；近义组收其他悬浮水的形态，以及表示更浓或更轻天气的词。

entries.definition: Full of mist, or seen as if through mist.
entries.definitionCN: 充满雾的；或像隔着一层雾看见的。

entries.definition: In a way that is blurred or covered with mist.
entries.definitionCN: 以朦胧或被雾遮住的方式。

entries.definition: The state of being misty or unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 有雾、朦胧的状态。

entries.definition: A light, fine drizzle; the spelling is close, but this word has its own origin.
entries.definitionCN: 细小的毛毛雨；拼写相近，但这个词另有来源。

entries.definition: Thicker cloud close to the ground that cuts visibility more sharply.
entries.definitionCN: 贴近地面、更浓的云雾，能见度下降得更厉害。

entries.definition: A light mist, often caused by heat or dust rather than by water alone.
entries.definitionCN: 轻薄的雾，常由热气或尘埃造成，不只是水汽。

entries.definition: Very light rain made of tiny drops.
entries.definitionCN: 由细小水滴构成的毛毛雨。

entries.definition: Hot vapour rising from boiling water that soon turns into droplets.
entries.definitionCN: 沸水升起的热汽，很快又凝成小水珠。

normalIntro.en: Old English used mist for dimness itself, and the family keeps describing what the eye cannot get through.
normalIntro.cn: 古英语用 mist 指「昏暗」本身，这个词族一直在描述眼睛穿不过去的东西。

normal.en: Old English mist named the dimness before it named droplets, so the word began with what the eye loses.
normal.cn: 古英语 mist 先指「昏暗」，后指水珠，所以这个词从「眼睛失去什么」开始。

normal.en: Misty adds -y and turns the noun into the felt quality of a morning.
normal.cn: misty 加 -y，把名词变成早晨能感觉到的那种质地。

normal.en: Mistiness stacks -ness on misty, making the quality itself into something you can name.
normal.cn: mistiness 在 misty 上再叠 -ness，把这种质地本身变成可以命名的东西。

normal.en: The verb mist over keeps the same droplets but moves them onto a surface, which is why a mirror and a valley use the same word.
normal.cn: 动词 mist over 保留同样的水珠，只把它们挪到表面上，所以镜子和山谷用同一个词。

normal.en: Fog, haze and mist differ in thickness and height, not in what they are made of.
normal.cn: fog、haze 与 mist 的差别在浓度和高度，而不在成分。

abstract.en: A word for dimness becomes a word for droplets, and the old feeling survives the new explanation.
abstract.cn: 一个表示昏暗的词变成表示水珠的词，旧的感觉在新解释里活了下来。

abstract.en: Mist on a field and mist in an eye both mean one thing: the distance has stopped being readable.
abstract.cn: 田野上的雾和眼睛里的雾意思相同：距离不再可读。

abstract.en: The smallest drops, too light to fall as rain, are enough to rename a whole morning.
abstract.cn: 小到还落不成雨的水珠，就足以给整个早晨换个名字。

examples.en: A thin mist lay over the lake at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时，湖面上浮着一层薄雾。

examples.en: The mirror misted over as the water ran hot.
examples.cn: 热水流下时，镜子蒙上了一层雾。

examples.en: She could not read the road through the mist.
examples.cn: 隔着那层雾，她看不清路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「觅丝」——雾像一层薄薄的丝，缠在眼前，让人「觅」不见路。

root: 古英语 mist（昏暗、雾），更早为重构的日耳曼语形式 *mihstaz；更远的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start from dim air near the ground and spread to any fine droplets, to a blur in the eye, and to the verb for a surface that fogs over.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从贴地的昏暗空气开始，扩散到任何细小的水珠，再到眼前的朦胧，最后到表示表面蒙雾的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey white veil floating on the lake, the far trees reduced to outlines.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨的湖面浮着一层灰白色的薄纱，对岸的树只剩轮廓。

branches.cn: 日出前被抹掉的田野

branches.en: a fountain throwing cool dust into the air
branches.cn: 喷泉把凉雾甩到空中

branches.en: eyes swimming before a word can be read
branches.cn: 话还没读完，眼睛先模糊

branches.en: a bathroom mirror losing its reflection
branches.cn: 浴室镜子丢掉自己的倒影

branches.en: weather and tears doing the same work to the eye
branches.cn: 天气和眼泪对眼睛做同一件事

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun for dim air, with English endings that turn it into an adjective, an adverb, a state and a verb.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示昏暗空气的名词，再加英语词尾，可以变成形容词、副词、状态名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mist; Latin words for fog, such as nebula, are different words with no shared origin.
latinIntro.cn: mist 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语中表示雾的词如 nebula 是另一个词，并无共同来源。
